metadata.title: On the estimation of high-dimensional integrated covariance matrices based on high-frequency data with multiple transactions

extraction_notes.note: Simulation designs (Design I/II, Settings I-IV), tables and empirical findings in Section 4 and the motivating L-averaging experiment in the Introduction were not extracted as nodes; only their numbered equations, the defined quantities and the stated conjecture/open problem were.
The NS estimator is presented as a definition built from an oracle optimization; extracted as an unmarked algorithm (like ANS and MNS) with the problem and its closed-form solution nested.
Cited results from Zheng & Li (2011) are stated loosely in single introduction sentences; extracted as external nodes with confidence below 1.
Proofs of Theorems 2.1-2.3 sit in supplement appendix sections without proof environments; the one-sentence reductions and the whole Appendix C were extracted as prose proofs.

nodes.name: Latent log price vector
nodes.statement: Suppose that we have $p$ stocks whose latent log price at time $t$ is denoted by ${\bf X}_t = (X_t^{(1)}, \cdots, X_t^{(p)})^\mathrm{T}$, where $T$ denotes the transpose.

nodes.name: Diffusion price model
nodes.statement_short: Log prices follow dX_t = mu_t dt + Theta_t dW_t with drift mu_t and covolatility process Theta_t.

nodes.name: Diffusion model SDE
nodes.statement: d{\bf X}_t = \boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt + \boldsymbol{\Theta}_td{\bf W}_t, \hspace{1cm} t\in [0,1],
nodes.label: eq: Model

nodes.name: Integrated covariance (ICV) matrix
ICV definition
nodes.statement: \textrm{ICV} :=\int_0^1 \boldsymbol{\Theta}_t\boldsymbol{\Theta}_t^\mathrm{T} dt
nodes.label: eq: definition of ICV

nodes.name: Realized covariance (RCV) matrix
nodes.statement:
The classical estimator of the ICV matrix is the so-called realized covariance (RCV) matrix, which is defined as follows. Suppose that we can observe the log price processes $\{X_{t_i}^{(j)}\}_{j=1}^p$ synchronously at recording time $t_i = i/n$, $i=0,1,\cdots,n$, during one trading day. Then the RCV matrix is defined as
\[\textrm{RCV} := \sum_{i=1}^n\Delta{\bf X}_i(\Delta{\bf X}_i)^{\mathrm{T}},\]
where
\[
\Delta{\bf X}_i = \begin{pmatrix}
\Delta X_i^{(1)}\\
\vdots \\
\Delta X_i^{(p)}\\
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
 X_{t_i}^{(1)} -  X_{t_{i-1}}^{(1)}\\
\vdots\\
 X_{t_i}^{(p)} -  X_{t_{i-1}}^{(p)}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: RCV is the sum of outer products of synchronous log-price increments over n equally spaced times.

nodes.name: Class C processes
nodes.statement: Suppose that $({\bf X}_t)$ is a $p$-dimensional process satisfying (\ref{eq: Model}) and $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_t$ is c\`{a}dl\`{a}g. Then $({\bf X}_t)$ belongs to class $\mathcal{C}$ if, almost surely, there exist $\gamma_t\in D([0,1]; \mathbb{R})$ and $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}$ a $p\times p$ matrix satisfying $\begin{rm}tr\end{rm}(\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^\mathrm{T}) = p$ such that \begin{equation} \bm\Theta_t = \gamma_t \bm \Lambda, \end{equation} where $D([0,1]; \mathbb{R})$ is the space of c\`{a}dl\`{a}g functions from $[0,1]$ to $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.statement_short: A diffusion is in class C if its covolatility factors as a scalar cadlag process times a fixed matrix with tr(Lambda Lambda^T)=p.

nodes.name: Covolatility factorization Theta_t = gamma_t Lambda
nodes.statement: \bm\Theta_t = \gamma_t \bm \Lambda,
nodes.label: eq: definition of Theta

nodes.name: Log prices belong to class C (Zheng-Li Proposition 4)
nodes.statement: It has been shown that the log price process $({\bf X}_t)$ belongs to class ${\mathcal C}$ in Proposition 4 of \cite{ZhengandLi2011}, with the reasonable assumption that the correlation structure of $({\bf X}_t)$ does not change over a short time period.
assumptions: the correlation structure of $({\bf X}_t)$ does not change over a short time period
conclusions: the log price process $({\bf X}_t)$ belongs to class ${\mathcal C}$

nodes.name: Time-variation adjusted realized covariance (TVA) matrix
nodes.statement:
Hence, an alternative estimator has been proposed, the time-variation adjusted realized covariance (TVA) matrix, which is defined as
\[
\textrm{TVA}:= \frac{\begin{rm} tr\end{rm}(\textrm{RCV})}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\Delta{\bf X}_i(\Delta{\bf X}_i)^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|\Delta{\bf X}_i|^2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: TVA rescales self-normalized increment outer products by tr(RCV)/n.

nodes.name: Zheng-Li Theorem 2: LSD of TVA via Marcenko-Pastur
nodes.statement:
Although the TVA matrix remains inconsistent, using random matrix theory,
Theorem 2 of \cite{ZhengandLi2011} shows that
its limiting spectral distribution depends solely on the ICV matrix through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation \eqref{eq: m-p equation} (see Theorem \ref{thm: theorem for the TVAPA}).
conclusions: its limiting spectral distribution depends solely on the ICV matrix through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation \eqref{eq: m-p equation}

nodes.name: Empirical spectral distribution (ESD)
nodes.statement:
From random matrix theory, for any $p$-dimensional symmetric matrix ${\bf A}$, the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) is defined as
\begin{eqnarray} F^{{\bf A}} (x) = \dfrac 1p \sum_{j=1}^p \ {\mathbf{I}} (\lambda_j({\bf A}) \le x), ~~~~ \forall x\in \mathbb{R},
\end{eqnarray}
where ${\mathbf{I}}(\cdot)$ is an indicator function and $\lambda_j({\bf A})$ denotes the $j$th largest eigenvalue of matrix ${\bf A}$.

nodes.name: ESD formula
nodes.statement: F^{{\bf A}} (x) = \dfrac 1p \sum_{j=1}^p \ {\mathbf{I}} (\lambda_j({\bf A}) \le x), ~~~~ \forall x\in \mathbb{R},
nodes.label: eqn:ESD

nodes.name: Limiting spectral distribution (LSD)
nodes.statement: The limit of ESD is referred to as the limiting spectral distribution (LSD), if it exists.

nodes.name: Number sets and upper half plane
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{Z}$, and $\mathbb{N}$ denote the sets of complex, real, integer, and natural numbers, respectively;  $\mathbb{C}^+$, a subset of $\mathbb{C}$, contains positive imaginary parts.

nodes.name: Euclidean norm notation
nodes.statement: All vectors are column vectors, and we use $|\cdot|$ to denote the Euclidean norm for vectors.

nodes.name: Spectral norm
nodes.statement: For any real matrix ${\bf A}$, $\|{\bf A}\| = \sqrt{\lambda_{\max}({\bf A}{\bf A}^{\mathrm{T}})}$ denotes its spectral norm, where $\lambda_{\max}$ is the largest eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Frobenius norm
nodes.statement: $||{\bf A}||_F = \sqrt{\begin{rm} tr\end{rm}({\bf A}{\bf A}^{{\mathrm{T}}})}$ denotes the Frobenius norm of matrix ${\bf A}$.

nodes.name: Stieltjes transform
nodes.statement:
For any distribution function $F$, $m_F(\cdot)$ denotes its Stieltjes transform defined as
\[m_F(z) = \int \frac{1}{\lambda - z}dF(\lambda), \hspace{1cm} \text{for~} z\in \mathbb{C}^+ :=\{z \in \mathbb{C}: \Im(z) > 0\},\]
where  $\Im(z)$ is the imaginary part of $z$, and
$\lfloor\cdot\rfloor$ indicates rounding down to the nearest integer.
nodes.statement_short: Stieltjes transform m_F(z) = int 1/(lambda - z) dF(lambda) on the upper half plane; also floor notation.

nodes.name: Multiple-transaction observation scheme
nodes.statement:
In a given time interval $[0,1]$, one trading day, for any process $({\bf V}_t)$,
suppose that $({\bf V}_t)$ can be observed at time points $t_i = i/n$ and there are $L_i (L_i\geq 1)$ transactions during each time interval $(t_{i - 1}, t_i]$, for $i = 1,\cdots, n$.

nodes.name: Transaction-level observations and times
nodes.statement:
Let $V_{T_{i-1}+j}$ be the $j$th observation at  transaction time $s_{T_{i-1}+j}$ during
time interval $(t_{i-1}, t_i]$ with $T_0\equiv 0$ and $T_i=\sum_{k=1}^i L_k$, for $j=1,2,\cdots,L_i$ and $i=1,2,\cdots, n$.

nodes.name: Averaged multiple-transaction price
nodes.statement:
One commonly used method to deal with multiple transactions involves taking averages of the multiple transaction prices at each time point $t_i$, that is,
\[
\overline{{\bf V}}_i = \dfrac{1}{L_i}
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i} {\bf V}_{T_{i-1}+j}, ~~~~~
i=1,\cdots,n,
\]
and using $\overline{{\bf V}}_i$ to approximate the observation at time point $t_i$.

nodes.name: Averaged increment and asymmetric triangular weights
nodes.statement:
Then the increment becomes
\begin{align}
\Delta\overline{\bf{V}}_i :&= \overline{\bf{V}}_i - \overline{\bf{V}}_{i-1}\notag \\
& = \frac{1}{L_i}\sum_{j=1}^{L_i} {\bf V}_{T_{i-1} + j} - \frac{1}{L_{i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}} {\bf V}_{T_{i-2}+ j}\notag\\
& = \frac{1}{L_i}\sum_{j=1}^{L_i} ({\bf V}_{T_{i-1}+j} - {\bf V}_{T_{i-2}}) - \frac{1}{L_{i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}} ({\bf V}_{T_{i-2} + j} - {\bf V}_{T_{i-2}} ) \\
& =  \sum_{j=1}^{L_i}a_{i,j}\Delta_{i ,j}{\bf V} + \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}}b_{i-1,j}\Delta_{i - 1,j}{\bf V}\notag,
\end{align}
where $a_{i,j} = 1-\frac{j-1}{L_i}$, $b_{i,j} = \frac{j-1}{L_i}$, and
\[
\Delta_{i,j}{\bf V} := {\bf V}_{T_{i-1}+j} - {\bf V}_{T_{i-1}+j-1}, ~\text{for}~~ j=1,\cdots, L_i, ~ i=1,\cdots,n,
\]
which is an asymmetric triangular form of $\Delta_{i,j}{\bf V}$.
nodes.statement_short: The averaged-price increment is a weighted sum of tick returns with weights a_{i,j}=1-(j-1)/L_i and b_{i,j}=(j-1)/L_i.

nodes.name: Averaged increment decomposition
nodes.label: eqn:Delta_V

nodes.name: Averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix
nodes.statement_short: ATVA: TVA built from non-overlapping averaged-price increments over N = n/2 pairs.

nodes.name: ATVA matrix formula
nodes.statement: {\mathcal A}_N := \dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^N |\Delta \overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}|^2}{N} \cdot \sum_{i=1}^N \dfrac{\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i} \Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}^T}{|\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}|^2} = \dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^N |\Delta \overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}|^2}{p} \cdot \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}},
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Class C price process
nodes.statement: For all $p$, $({\bf X}_t)$ is a $p$-dimensional process in class $\mathcal{C}$ for some drift process $\boldsymbol{\mu}_t = (\mu_t^{(1)},\cdots,\mu_t^{(p)})^{\mathrm{T}}$ and covolatility process $(\boldsymbol{\Theta}_t) = (\gamma_t\boldsymbol{\Lambda})$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Bounded drift
nodes.statement: there exists a $C_0<\infty$ such that for all $p$ and all $l = 1,\cdots,p$, $|\mu_t^{(l)}|\leq C_0$ for all $t\in[0,1)$ almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Bounded gamma with limited dependence on W
nodes.statement: there exists a $0\leq \delta_1<1/2$ and a sequence of index sets $\mathcal{I}_p$ satisfying $\mathcal{I}_p \subset \{1,\cdots, p\}$ and $\#\mathcal{I}_p = O(p^{\delta_1})$ such that $(\gamma_t)$ may depend on ${\bf W}_t$ but only on $(W_t^{(l)}:l\in \mathcal{I}_p)$; moreover, there exists a $C_1<\infty$ such that for all $p$, $|\gamma_t|\in(1/C_1, C_1)$ for all $t\in [0,1)$, almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Bounded individual volatilities
nodes.statement: there exists $C_2<\infty$ such that for all $p$ and all $l$, the individual volatilities $\sigma_t^{(l)} = \sqrt{(\gamma_t)^2\sum_{k=1}^p(\Lambda_{lk})^2}\in (1/C_2, C_2)$ for all $t\in [0,1]$ almost surely; in addition, $(\gamma_t)$ converges uniformly to a nonzero process $(\gamma_t^*)$ that is piecewise continuous with finitely many jumps almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: ICV spectral norm growth bound
nodes.statement: there exists $C_3<\infty$ and $0\leq \delta_2 <1/2$ such that for all $p$, $||\text{ICV}|| \leq C_3p^{\delta_2}$ almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: delta_1 + delta_2 < 1/2
nodes.statement: the $\delta_1$ in \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma} and $\delta_2$ in \eqref{asm:bdd_ICV} satisfy that $\delta_1 + \delta_2 <1/2$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: ESD of Lambda Lambda^T converges
nodes.statement: almost surely, as $p\to\infty$, the ESD of $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{T}}$ converges in distribution to a probability distribution $\breve{H}$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Dimension ratio p/N -> rho
nodes.statement: $N = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ with $\lim_{p\to \infty} p/N \to \rho \in (0, \infty)$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Equally spaced transaction durations
nodes.statement: the transaction durations are equally spaced in each time interval $(t_{i-1}, t_i]$, that is, $\Delta s_{i,j}: = s_{T_{i-1}+j} - s_{T_{i-1}+j-1} = 1/(nL_i)$ for $j = 1,\cdots, L_i$ and $i = 1,\cdots, n$;
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Independent transaction counts with moment functions
nodes.statement: $\{L_{1},\cdots, L_n\}$ is a sequence of independent positive integers independent of $({\bf X}_t)$ with $E(\frac{1}{L_i}) = f_{1, t_i}$ and $E(\frac{1}{L_i^2}) = f_{2, t_i}$ for $i = 1, \cdots, n$, where $f_{1, t}$ and $f_{2, t}$ are c\`{a}dl\`{a}g functions satisfying $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} f_{1, t} = f_{1, t}^*$, $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} f_{2, t} = f_{2, t}^*$ for $t\in [0,1]$.
nodes.section: 2.1 LSD of non-overlapping averaged TVA (ATVA) matrix

nodes.name: Stationary rho-mixing noise
nodes.statement: For all $j= 1,\cdots,p$, the noise $(\varepsilon_t^{(j)})$ is a stationary time series with mean 0 and has bounded $4\ell$th moments and $\rho$-mixing coefficients $\rho^{(j)}(r)$ satisfying $\max_{j=1,\cdots,p} \rho^{(j)}(r) = O(r^{-\ell})$ for some integer $\ell>2$;
nodes.section: 2.2 Pre-averaging averaged TVA (PA-ATVA) matrix in the presence of microstructure noise

nodes.name: Pre-averaging window size
nodes.statement: $h =\lfloor \xi n^{\beta} \rfloor$ for some $\xi\in(0,\infty)$ and $\beta \in ((3+\ell)/(2\ell +2), 1)$, and $M = \lfloor n/(2h)\rfloor$ satisfy that $\lim_{p\to\infty} p/M = c >0$, where $\ell$ is the integer in Assumption \eqref{asm:error};
nodes.section: 2.2 Pre-averaging averaged TVA (PA-ATVA) matrix in the presence of microstructure noise

nodes.name: Bounded number of transactions
nodes.statement: there exists a constant $L^*<\infty$ such that  $\sup\limits_{1\leq i \leq n} L_i\leq L^*$, almost surely;
nodes.section: 2.2 Pre-averaging averaged TVA (PA-ATVA) matrix in the presence of microstructure noise

nodes.name: Last transaction times approach grid
nodes.statement: $\max\limits_{1\leq i \leq n} n(s_{T_i} - s_{T_{i-1}}) \to 1$, almost surely, as $n\to \infty$.

nodes.name: LSD of ATVA matrix under multiple transactions
nodes.statement: Suppose that Assumptions \eqref{asm:class_c}--\eqref{asm:moment_L} hold. Then, almost surely, the ESDs of ICV and ${\mathcal A}_N$ converge to probability distributions $H$ and $F^{{\mathcal A}}$, respectively, where \begin{equation} H(x)=\breve{H}(x/\theta), ~~~ \textrm{for all } x\geq 0 ~ \textrm{with} ~ \theta=\int_0^1 (\gamma_t^*)^2 dt, \end{equation} and $F^{{\mathcal A}}$ and $H$ are related as follows: \[ m_{{\mathcal A}}(z) = \int_{\tau\in \mathbb{R}} \frac{1}{\tilde{\theta}_f/\theta\cdot\tau(1 - \rho(1 + zm_{{\mathcal A}}(z))) - z}dH(\tau), ~~~~ \textrm{for} ~ z\in \mathbb{C}^+, \] where $\tilde{\theta}_f = \int_0^1 (\dfrac 13 + \dfrac 16 f_{2,s}^*)(\gamma_s^*)^2ds$ and $m_{{\mathcal A}}(z)$ denotes the Stieltjes transform of $F^{{\mathcal A}}$.

nodes.name: ICV factorization and inconsistency of the TVA scale
nodes.statement: Note that if $({\bf X}_t)$ belongs to class $\mathcal{C}$ then the ICV matrix can be written as $\textrm{ICV} = \int_0^1 \gamma_t^2 dt\cdot \breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$, where $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{T}}$. When $L_i \equiv 1$, Theorem 2 of \cite{ZhengandLi2011} shows that the LSDs of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ and $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ are related through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation (see \eqref{eq: converfence of proposition A1}), and $2\sum_{i=1}^N|\Delta {\bf X}_{2i}|^2/p $ is a consistent estimator of $\theta=\int_0^1 (\gamma_t^*)^2 dt$. Throughout the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:LSD_TVA} in this paper, the LSDs of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ and $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ are related through the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur equation (see Proposition \ref{prop: convergence of tilde sigma} in the appendix); however, $2\sum_{i=1}^N|\Delta {\bf X}_{2i}|^2/p $ is no longer consistent with $\theta$ in a general setting when $L_i \equiv 1$ is not satisfied. Hence, a non-overlapping A-ATVA matrix, $\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}_N$, is proposed in Corollary \ref{cor:LSD_ATVA}, the LSD of which depends solely on that of the ICV matrix.

nodes.statement_short: For class C, ICV = theta * Lambda Lambda^T; the TVA scale estimator is inconsistent unless L_i = 1, motivating the A-ATVA matrix.

nodes.name: U-shaped intraday volatility and piecewise constant moments
nodes.statement: Moreover, observe that the stock intraday volatility tends to be U-shaped, which implies that the numbers of transactions at opening and closing of the market tend to be much larger than the numbers in the middle of the day. Thus, if Assumption \eqref{asm:moment_L} is further taken to be piecewise constant, Corollary \ref{cor:LSD_ATVA} (see below) holds.

nodes.name: Adjusted ATVA (A-ATVA) matrix
nodes.statement:
If we further suppose that $(f_{2, s}^*)$ is piecewise constant, that is, there exist constant numbers  $\eta_1,\cdots,\eta_K$ for $K<\infty$ such that
\[
f_{2, s}^* = \sum_{i=1}^K \eta_i  \mathrm{I}\{s\in(a_{i-1}, a_i]\},
\]
where $(0, 1] = \sum_{i =1}^K (a_{i-1}, a_i]$ and $0 = a_{0} <a_1<\cdots<a_K = 1$, then we define the adjusted ATVA (A-ATVA) matrix as
\[
\widetilde{{\mathcal A}}_N := \frac{1}{p}\sum_{i = 1}^K \left( \dfrac13 + \frac{1}{6(\ell_i - \ell_{i-1})}\sum_{j = \ell_{i-1}+1}^{\ell_i}\frac{1}{L_j^2}\right)^{-1} \sum_{m = \lfloor (\ell_{i-1} + 1)/2\rfloor + 1}^{\lfloor\ell_i/2\rfloor}|\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2m}|^2
\cdot \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}},
\]
where $\ell_i = \max\limits_{0\leq j\leq n}j/n\leq a_i$, provided that $\min\limits_{1\leq i \leq K}n(a_i - a_{i-1})\geq 3$.

nodes.statement_short: A-ATVA rescales ATVA piecewise by the inverse of 1/3 + (1/6)·mean(1/L_j^2), correcting the multiple-transaction bias.

nodes.name: Nonlinear shrinkage (NS) estimator
nodes.statement:
Suppose that we observe high-frequency multiple noisy observations $\{{\bf Y}_{t_i}\}$ during time period $[T - \tau, T]$ at current time $T$, for $\tau\geq 1$.
We construct matrix $\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}$ based on observations $\{{\bf Y}_{t_i}\}$ over time period $[T - \tau ,T]$ and estimator $\hat\theta_p$ based on observations $\{{\bf Y}_{t_i}\}$ during time interval $[T - 1, T]$.
We denote the spectral decomposition of matrix $\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}$ by
\[
\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T}\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_{T - \tau, T} \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T}^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
where the eigenmatrix $\widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[1], \cdots, \widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[p])$, whose $i$th column is the eigenvector of $\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}} $, and $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_{T - \tau, T} = \textrm{diag} \{ \widetilde{\lambda}_1 ,\cdots,  \widetilde{\lambda}_p\}$ is a diagonal matrix with non-increasing eigenvalues $\widetilde{\lambda}_1\geq \cdots \geq \widetilde{\lambda}_p$.
To construct an NS estimator of $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$, we retain the eigenmatrix $\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T}$ and consider a class of estimators of the form:
\[
\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T} {\bf D} \widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T}^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
where $D = \textrm{diag}( d_1, \cdots,  d_p)$ is diagonal.
In order to measure the distance between two matrices, we adopt the Frobenius norm.
The objective is to find the diagonal matrix ${\bf D}$ that solves the optimization problem
\[
\min\limits_{{\bf D} ~~\text{diag}}\| \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T} {\bf D} \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T}^{{\mathrm{T}}} - \breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}\|_F.
\]
By elementary calculation, the solution is
\[D^{or} = \textrm{diag}(d_1^{or},\cdots, d_p^{or}),
\]
where
\begin{equation} d_i^{or} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[i])^{{\mathrm{T}}} \breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} \widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[i].
\end{equation}
Therefore, we propose the following nonlinear shrinkage (NS) estimator for ICV:
\[
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{NS}: = \hat{\theta}_p \cdot \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{NS},
\]
where $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{NS} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T} \textrm{diag}(\widehat{d_1^{or}},\cdots, \widehat{d_p^{or}}) \widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau ,T}^{{\mathrm{T}}}$,
and $\widehat{d_i^{or}}$ is an estimator of $d_i^{or}$, solved by the algorithm proposed by \cite{LedoitandWolf2017}.
input: high-frequency multiple noisy observations $\{{\bf Y}_{t_i}\}$ during time period $[T - \tau, T]$ at current time $T$
nodes.statement_short: Keep eigenvectors of Xi~, replace eigenvalues by Frobenius-optimal oracle values estimated via Ledoit-Wolf, scale by theta-hat.

\]
nodes.statement_short: Choose diagonal D minimizing the Frobenius distance between U D U^T and Lambda Lambda^T.

nodes.name: Averaged nonlinear shrinkage (ANS) estimator
nodes.statement:
Suppose that we have tick-by-tick high-frequency observations $\{{\bf Y}_{l_i}\}$ over time period $[T - \tau, T]$ at current time $T$.
First, the estimator $\hat{\theta}_p = 3\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2/p$ can be established based on high-frequency data during time interval $[T - 1, T]$.
Suppose that there are in total $M_{\tau} = \tau \cdot M$ averaged noisy increments $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2j}, j = 1, \cdots, M_{\tau}$, over time period $[T - \tau, T]$, in which the overnight increments are excluded and there are $M$ increments each day.
Next, we permute the increments $B$ times.
At the $k$th permutation, we split the increments $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}$ into two parts, say $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)} = (\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_1, \Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_2)$, for $k = 1,\cdots, B$, with $\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^{(k)}_\ell$ having size $p\times M_{\tau_{\ell}}$ $(\ell = 1, 2)$ and $M_{\tau_1} + M_{\tau_2} = M_{\tau}$.
We define
\[
\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}_{\ell}^{(k)} := \frac{p}{M_{\tau_{\ell}}}\sum_{i \in J_{\ell, k}}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i} (\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i})^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2},
\]
where $J_{\ell, k} = \{i: \Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i} \in \Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{\ell}^{(k)}\}$ for $\ell = 1, 2$ and $k = 1, \cdots, B$.
We denote the spectral decomposition of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_1^{(k)}$ as
\[
\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_1^{(k)} = \widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)}\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_1^{(k)}(\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)})^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
for $k = 1,\cdots, B$.
Then the averaged nonlinear shrinkage (ANS) estimator of ICV is defined as
\begin{equation*}
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{\textrm{ANS}}:= \hat{\theta}_p\cdot\frac{1}{B} \sum_{k=1}^B \widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}^{(k)}_{\textrm{ANS}}, ~~\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}^{(k)}_{\textrm{ANS}} = \widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)} \textrm{diag}((\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)})^{{\mathrm{T}}} \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_2^{(k)}\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)}) (\widetilde{\bf U}_1^{(k)})^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\end{equation*}
where $\textrm{diag}({\bf A})$ sets all non-diagonal elements of matrix ${\bf A}$ to zero.
To this end, $M_{\tau_1}$ is chosen using the following criterion,
\begin{equation}\arg\min\limits_{M_{\tau_1}\in \mathcal{G}} \bigg| \bigg|  \frac{1}{B} \sum_{k = 1}^B (\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}^{(k)}_{\textrm{ANS}} -  \widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}_2^{(k)}) \bigg| \bigg|_F^2, \end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\mathcal{G} = \bigg[2M_{\tau}^{1/2}, 0.2M_{\tau}, 0.4M_{\tau},
0.6M_{\tau}, 0.8M_{\tau},
 M_{\tau} - 2.5M_{\tau}^{1/2}, M_{\tau} - 1.5M_{\tau}^{1/2}\bigg]
\end{split} \end{equation}
is the candidate set for $M_{\tau_1}$, recommended by \cite{Lam2016} and \cite{Lametal2017}.
input: tick-by-tick high-frequency observations $\{{\bf Y}_{l_i}\}$ over time period $[T - \tau, T]$ at current time $T$
nodes.statement_short: Permute and split pre-averaged increments B times; use eigenvectors from one part and eigenvalue estimates from the other, average, scale by theta-hat.

nodes.label: eq: nonlinear shrnkage criterion

nodes.name: Mixed nonlinear shrinkage (MNS) estimator
nodes.statement:
Suppose that we observe high-frequency data $\{{\bf Y}_t\}$ with multiple transactions during time period $[T - \tau, T]$.
First, the matrix $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{T-\tau, T-1}$ in \eqref{eq: definition of hbSigma} is constructed based on high-frequency data during time period $[T - \tau, T - 1]$, and its spectral decomposition is denoted as
\[
\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{T-\tau, T - 1} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T - 1}\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}_{T-\tau, T - 1}(\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T - 1})^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
where
\[
\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T - 1} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[1], \cdots, \widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[p]).
\]
Second, we set the eigenvectors $\widetilde{\bf u}_{T-\tau, T - 1}[k]$, $k = 1,\cdots, p$, to be given beforehand, and transform the averaged high-frequency data $\{\overline{{\bf Y}}_i\}$ during time period $[T - 1, T]$.

\[

\]

\[
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{\textrm{MNS}} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T -\tau, T -1} \textrm{diag} (\widehat{d_1^{\textrm{APA}}}, \cdots, \widehat{d_p^{\textrm{APA}}})\widetilde{\bf U}_{T -\tau, T -1}^{{\mathrm{T}}}.
\]

We denote the spectral decomposition of matrix $\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}$ by
\[

\]

nodes.name: Restrict to rotation-equivariant class
nodes.statement:
To construct an NS estimator of $\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$, we retain the eigenmatrix $\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T}$ and consider a class of estimators of the form:
\[
\widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T} {\bf D} \widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau, T}^{{\mathrm{T}}},
\]
where $D = \textrm{diag}( d_1, \cdots,  d_p)$ is diagonal.

nodes.name: Solve oracle Frobenius problem
nodes.statement:
In order to measure the distance between two matrices, we adopt the Frobenius norm.
The objective is to find the diagonal matrix ${\bf D}$ that solves the optimization problem
\[
\min\limits_{{\bf D} ~~\text{diag}}\| \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T} {\bf D} \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T}^{{\mathrm{T}}} - \breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}\|_F.
\]
By elementary calculation, the solution is
\[D^{or} = \textrm{diag}(d_1^{or},\cdots, d_p^{or}),
\]
where
\begin{equation} d_i^{or} = (\widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[i])^{{\mathrm{T}}} \breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} \widetilde{\bf u}_{T - \tau, T}[i].
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Form NS estimator via Ledoit-Wolf
nodes.statement:

\[

\]
where $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{NS} = \widetilde{\bf U}_{T - \tau, T} \textrm{diag}(\widehat{d_1^{or}},\cdots, \widehat{d_p^{or}}) \widetilde{\bf U}_{T-\tau ,T}^{{\mathrm{T}}}$,
and $\widehat{d_i^{or}}$ is an estimator of $d_i^{or}$, solved by the algorithm proposed by \cite{LedoitandWolf2017}.

nodes.statement: Recall that \[\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i} = \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}\Delta_{2i,j}{\bf X} + \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}\Delta_{2i-1,j}{\bf X},\] where $a_{i,j} = 1-\frac{j-1}{L_i}, b_{i,j} = \frac{j-1}{L_i}$, and $\Delta_{i,j}{\bf X} = {\bf X}_{T_{i-1}+j} - {\bf X}_{T_{i-1}+j - 1}$. Then we separate $\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}$ into two parts, \begin{equation} \Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i} = \sqrt{w_i}(\boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_{i} + {\bf V}_i), \end{equation} where \begin{equation} w_i = \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1}}^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j}}\gamma_t^2dt + \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\int_{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j}}\gamma_t^2dt, \end{equation} \[{\bf Z}_i = \frac{1}{\sqrt{w_i}}\left[\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1} }^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j} }\gamma_td{\bf W}_t + \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}\int_{s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{s_{T_{2i-2} + j} }\gamma_td{\bf W}_t \right],\] and \[{\bf V}_i = \frac{1}{\sqrt{w_i}}\left[\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1} }^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j} }\boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt + \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}\int_{s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{s_{T_{2i-2} + j} }\boldsymbol{\mu}_tdt \right].\] Using the above notation, $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ can be rewritten as \[\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} = \frac{p}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2} = \frac{p}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \frac{({\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i)({\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i)^{\mathrm{T}} }{|{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i|^2}.\] Notice that \[ \frac{1}{L_{2i}} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}} a_{2i,j} = \frac{1}{2}(1 + \frac{1}{L_{2i}}), ~~ \frac{1}{L_{2i - 1}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i - 1}} b_{2i-1, j} = \frac{1}{2}(1 - \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}) \] and \[ \frac{1}{L_{2i}} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}} a_{2i,j}^2 = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6L_{2i}^2} + \frac{1}{2L_{2i}}, ~\frac{1}{L_{2i - 1}} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i - 1}} b_{2i - 1,j}^2 = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6L_{2i - 1}^2} - \frac{1}{2L_{2i-1}}, \] which are all uniformly bounded as $L_i \geq 1$. By the boundedness of $|\mu_t^{(l)}|$ and $|\gamma_t|$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu} and \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma}, and the equally spaced transaction durations $\Delta s_{i,j}$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_duration}, there exists $C>0$ such that $|{\bf V}_i^{(l)}|\leq C/\sqrt{N}$ for all $i=1,\cdots,N,l=1,\cdots, p$, which indicates that the $|{\bf V}_i|$ are uniformly bounded. By a similar argument to that used in (3.34) in \cite{ZhengandLi20112}, we have \begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq N} \big|\frac{1}{p}|\boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i|^2-1\big| \to 0, \hspace{0.5cm} \text{almost surely}. \end{equation} By the boundedness of the $|{\bf V}_i|$, we further have \begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq N} \big|\frac{1}{p}|{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i|^2-1\big| \to 0, \hspace{0.5cm} \text{almost surely}. \end{equation} By the same arguments used in the proof of Theorem 2 in \cite{ZhengandLi20112}, we can show that Proposition \ref{prop: convergence of tilde sigma} holds.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$

otin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{ rac{2i-2}{n}}^{ rac{2i}{n}}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds\ := &D_1 + D_2.\ \end{split} \end{equation*} As $(N w_{\ell_j})$, $|\gamma_s^*|$, and $|f_{2,s}^*|$ are bounded, for any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, we have \[|D_1|\leq  rac{2}{n}JC <\epsilon.\] Notice that \[ E \left( rac{1}{L_{2i}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 ight)=  rac{1}{3} +  rac{1}{6}E ig( rac{1}{L_{2i}^2} ig) +  rac{1}{2}E ig( rac{1}{L_{2i}} ig), \] and \[ E\left(  rac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1 ,j}^2 ight) =  rac{1}{3} +  rac{1}{6} E ig(  rac{1}{L_{2i-1}^2} ig) -  rac{1}{2} E ig(  rac{1}{L_{2i-1}} ig). \] For the second term $D_2$, because $(\gamma_t^*)$, $f_{1,s}^*$, and $f_{2,s}^*$ are continuous in $[(2i-2)/n, 2i/n]$ when $i 
otin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}$, and by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_ICV} and \eqref{asm:moment_L}, $(\gamma_t)$, $(f_{1,s})$, and $(f_{2,s})$ uniformly converge to $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$, and $(f_{2,s}^*)$, respectively. For any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n,p$, we have \[|\gamma_t^* - \gamma_{2i/n}|<\epsilon, ~~ 	ext{and}~~ |f_{2, 2i/n}^* - f_{2, t}^*|<\epsilon, ~~ 	ext{for all} ~~t \in [ rac{2i-2}{n}, rac{2i}{n} ],\] for $i = 1,\cdots, N$ and $|\gamma_t - \gamma_t^*|<\epsilon$ for all $t\in [0,1]$. Define \[  egin{split} w_i^* &= \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1}}^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j}}(\gamma_t^*)^2dt + \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\int_{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j}}(\gamma_t^*)^2dt,\ \widetilde{w}_i^*&= (\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2  rac{1}{nL_{2i}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 + (\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2  rac{1}{nL_{2i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\ 	ext{and}~~~ \widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^*&=(\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2\cdot rac{2}{n} igg( rac{1}{3} +  rac{1}{6}f_{2, 2i/n}^* igg). \end{split} \] For all large $n$, because $|\gamma_t|\leq C$ and $1\leq L_i< L^*$, for any $i, t$, we have \[  egin{split} &|D_2| \ \leq& \sum\limits_{i}\int_{ rac{2i-2}{n}}^{ rac{2i}{n}}N|E(w_i) - E(w_i^*)|ds + \sum\limits_{i
otin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{ rac{2i-2}{n}}^{ rac{2i}{n}}N| E(w_i^*) - E(\widetilde{w}_i^*)|ds \ +&\sum\limits_{i}\int_{ rac{2i-2}{n}}^{ rac{2i}{n}}| NE(\widetilde{w}_i^*) - N\widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^*|ds +\sum\limits_{i
otin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{ rac{2i-2}{n}}^{ rac{2i}{n}}| N\widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^* - w_s|ds\ 	o& 0, ~~~	ext{almost surely.} \end{split} \] This completes the proof of \eqref{eq: convergence of Vi plus lambda Zi}.\hspace{ ill}$ lacksquare$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.2
nodes.statement:
Note that \[\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{ f{Y}}}_{2i}|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{ f{X}}}_{2i}|^2 + 2\sum_{i=1}^M\Delta\widetilde{\overline{ f{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{ m{\varepsilon}}}_{2i} + \sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{ m{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}|^2. \] The convergence of \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x} implies that $\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta \widetilde{\overline{ m{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}|^2/p 	o 0$ almost surely. It remains to prove that  egin{equation} \lim_{p	o\infty} 3 rac{\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{ f{X}}}_{2i}|^2}{p} = 	heta, \hspace{1cm} 	ext{almost surely}, \end{equation} and  egin{equation}  rac{\sum_{i=1}^M\Delta\widetilde{\overline{ f{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{ m{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}}{p}	o 0, \hspace{1cm}	ext{almost surely}. \end{equation} To show \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}, by \eqref{eq: psii plus error term}, it suffices to show that \[ \lim_{n	o\infty}\sum_{i=1}^M\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i -  rac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds =0, \] almost surely. Suppose that $\gamma_t^*$ has $J$ jumps at $\{	au_1,\cdots,	au_J\}$; then  egin{align*} &\sum_{i=1}^M\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} |M\psi_i -  rac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds\ =&\sum\limits_{i \in \{	au_1,\cdots,	au_J\}}\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i -  rac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds \ &+ \sum\limits_{i 
otin \{	au_1,\cdots,	au_J\}}\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i -  rac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds \ := &\Delta_1 + \Delta_2. \end{align*} For any $\epsilon > 0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, $|\Delta_1| \leq \epsilon$ follows from the boundedness of $|M\psi_i|$ and $\gamma_t^*$. For the second term, $\Delta_2$, by defining $\psi_i^*$ by replacing $\gamma_t$ with $\gamma_t^*$ from the definition of $\psi_i$, we have \[ |\Delta_2| \leq \Delta_{21} + \Delta_{22} + \Delta_{23} +\Delta_{24}, \] where \[  egin{split} \Delta_{21} &:= \sum\limits_{i 
otin \{	au_1, \cdots, 	au_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} |M\psi_i - M\psi_i^*|ds,\ \Delta_{22} &:= \sum\limits_{i 
otin \{	au_1, \cdots, 	au_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M\psi_i^* - M(\gamma_{(2i-2)/h}^*)^2A_i|ds,\ \Delta_{23} &:= \sum\limits_{i 
otin \{	au_1, \cdots, 	au_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M(\gamma_{(2i-2)/h}^*)^2A_i - M(\gamma_{s}^*)^2A_i |ds,\ \Delta_{24} &:= \sum\limits_{i 
otin \{	au_1, \cdots, 	au_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M(\gamma_{s}^*)^2A_i -  rac{1}{3}(\gamma_{s}^*)^2 |ds, \end{split} \] and \[  egin{split} A_i := & rac{1}{h^2} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}} a_{2ih,j}^2 \Delta s_{2ih,j} + \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \Big[1 -  rac{|h-l+1|}{h}+ \ &\hspace{1cm}+ rac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h}b_{(2i-2)h+l,j} \Big]^2\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} . \end{split} \] We further decompose $A_i$ as $A_i = A_{i1} + A_{i2} + A_{i3}+ A_{i4}$, where  egin{align*} A_{i1} &:=  rac{1}{h^2} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}} a_{2ih,j}^2 \Delta s_{2ih,j} = O( rac{1}{nh^2}),\ A_{i2} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \left(1 -  rac{|h-l+1|}{h} ight)^2\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j}=  rac{2h}{3n} + o( rac{h}{n}),\ A_{i3} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}  rac{2}{h}\left(1 -  rac{|h-l+1|}{h} ight)(|h-l+1| - |h-l|) \ &\cdot b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} = O( rac{1}{n}),\ A_{i4} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}  rac{1}{h^2}(|h-l+1| - |h-l|)^2b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^2\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} \ &= O( rac{1}{nh}), \end{align*} follow from the boundedness of $L_i$ both below and above, and $\Delta s_{i,j} = O(1/n)$ by Assumption \eqref{asm:interval}. As $(\gamma_t^*)$ is continuous in $[s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}, s_{T_{2ih}}]$ when $i 
otin \{	au_1, \cdots, 	au_J\}$, $(\gamma_t)$ uniformly converges to $(\gamma_t^*)$ by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_sigma}, and $\psi_i^* = O(h/n)$ by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma} and \eqref{asm:bdd_L}, for any $\epsilon >0 $ and sufficiently large $n,p$, it is easy to show that \[ |MA_i - 1/3|\leq \epsilon ~~~	ext{and}~~~\max\{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{22}, \Delta_{23},\Delta_{24} \}<C\epsilon. \] This completes the proof of \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}. Finally, \eqref{eq: twbX plus twbe} follows from \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx} and \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x}.\hspace{ ill}$ lacksquare$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.3
nodes.statement:
Without of generality, we may assume that  $\gamma_t$ is independent of ${\bf W}_t$.
Suppose that we have $L_i^{(q)}(\geq 1)$ observations for each stock $q$ at recording time $t_i = i/n$, for $q = 1,2,\cdots, p$ and $i = 1,2,\cdots, n$.
Recall that for any process $({\bf V}_t)$, $V_{i,j}^{(q)}$ denote the observation of the $j$th transaction for stock $q$ during time interval $(t_{i-1}, t_i]$,
and the true transaction time of $V_{i,j}^{(q)}$ is denoted as $s_{T_{i-1}+j}^{(q)}$, for $j = 1,\cdots, L_i^{(q)}$ satisfying $t_{i-1} \leq s_{T_{i-1}}^{(q)}< s_{T_{i-1} + 1}^{(q)}<\cdots < s_{T_{i-1} + L_i^{(q)}}^{(q)} = s_{T_i}^{(q)} \leq t_i$.
Under asynchronous trading conditions, the average of multiple observations at each recording time $t_i$ is denoted by
\[
\overline{\bf{V}}^*_i := \left(\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(1)}}\frac{1}{L_i^{(1)}}V_{i,j}^{(1)}, \cdots, \sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(p)}}\frac{1}{L_i^{(p)}}V_{i,j}^{(p)} \right)^{{\mathrm{T}}};
\]
thus, the increment at trading time $t_i$ becomes
\[\Delta\overline{{\bf V}}^*_i :=  \begin{pmatrix}
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(1)}}a_{i,j}^{(1)}\Delta_{i,j}^{(1)}V +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}^{(1)}}b_{i-1,j}^{(1)}\Delta_{i-1,j}^{(1)}V\\
\vdots\\
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(p)}}a_{i,j}^{(p)}\Delta_{i,j}^{(p)}V +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}^{(p)}}b_{i-1,j}^{(p)}\Delta_{i-1,j}^{(p)}V\\
\end{pmatrix},\]
where $a_{i,j}^{(q)} = 1 - \frac{j-1}{L_i^{(q)}}$, $b_{i,j}^{(q)} =  \frac{j-1}{L_i^{(q)}}$ and  $\Delta_{i,j}^{(q)}X = X_{i, j}^{(q)} -  X_{i, j-1}^{(q)}$, for $q = 1,2,\cdots,p$.
Similar to the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:LSD ttSigma}, we first show that
there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for large $M$
\begin{equation} \min\limits_{1\leq i\leq M} |\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}^*_{2i}|^2 \geq C,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq j \leq p} \sqrt{p}|\Delta (\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}^{*})^{(j)} | \to 0, ~~~\text{almost surely,}
\end{equation}
which leads to the result that the PA-ATVA matrix based on noisy observations $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^*_{2i}$ and that based on latent log price $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}^*_{2i}$ have the same LSD.
We only need to prove \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT}, as \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT done} holds straightforwardly from the proof of \eqref{eq: sqrtt p delta twbe} given earlier.
By a similar decomposition to that used in \eqref{eq: expression for tbwX}, the return based on the pre-averaged (latent) price can be decomposed as
\[
\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^* = \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-1)h+j}^* - \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+j}^* = {\bf R}_{i1} + {\bf M}_{i} + {\bf R}_{i2},
\]
where ${\bf M}_i = (M_{i}^{(1)}, \cdots, M_{i}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$, ${\bf R}_{i\ell} = (R_{i\ell}^{(1)}, \cdots, R_{i\ell}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$ for $\ell = 1, 2$, and their $q$th components have the form
\begin{align*}
R_{i1}^{(q)} = &\frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}^{(q)}}a_{2ih,j}^{(q)}\Delta_{2ih,j}^{(q)}X,\\
M_{i}^{(q)} = & \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}^{(q)} }c_{l,h} \Delta_{(2i-2)h + l,j}^{(q)}X,\\
R_{i2}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}^{(q)}} \left[ \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h}
b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^{(q)}\right]\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^{(q)} X,
\end{align*}
where $c_{l,h} = 1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} $.
Note that $M_i^{(q)}$ can be reduced to
\[
\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} \cdot (X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)}}^{(q)} - X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l - 1} }^{(q)}}^{(q)}).
\]
We further decompose $M_i^{(q)}$ as $W_i^{(q)} + R_{i3}^{(q)}$, where
\begin{align*}
W_{i}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} (X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l}}^{(q)} -  X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l - 1}}^{(q)}),\\
R_{i3}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} \left(  X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)}}^{(q)} - X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)} + X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l -1}}^{(q)} -  X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l - 1}}^{(q)}}^{(q)}  \right),
\end{align*}
and $X_{t_i}^{(q)}$ denotes the log price for stock $q$ at recording time $t_i$.  Let ${\bf W}_i = (W_{i}^{(1)}, \cdots, W_{i}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$, ${\bf R}_{i3} = (R_{i3}^{(1)}, \cdots, R_{i3}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$.
Thus, $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^*  = {\bf W}_i + {\bf R}_{i1} + {\bf R}_{i2}  + {\bf R}_{i3} $.
As 
\[{\bf W}_{i} = \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) \Delta {\bf X}_{(2i-2)h + l}^*,
\]
and 
\[
\Delta {\bf X}_{(2i-2)h + l}^* = \begin{pmatrix}
X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l }}}^{(1)} -X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l-1 }}}^{(1)}\\
 \vdots\\
  X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l }}}^{(p)} -X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l-1 }}}^{(p)}\\
  \end{pmatrix},
\]
it reduces to the synchronous setting.
Using a similar argument to that in \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}, we have
\[ \lim\limits_{p\to\infty} \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p} = \theta.
\]
Thus, \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT} follows if we can show that there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for large $M$
\begin{equation} \min\limits_{1\leq i \leq M}|{\bf W}_{i}|^2\geq C,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq q \leq p}\sqrt{p}|R_{i1}^{(q)} + R_{i2}^{(q)} +  R_{i3}^{(q)}|\to 0,~~~\text{almost surely.}
\end{equation}
Hence, the PA-ATVA matrix based on noisy observations $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}^*_{2i}$ and that based on latent log price $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}^*_{2i}$ have the same LSD.
Further, using \eqref{eq: min of Wi2}, \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}, and Lemma \ref{lem: appendix B lemma 1}, we obtain that
\[
3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}{p} \cdot \frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^* (\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*)^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}
~~\text{and}~~3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p}\cdot\frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{{\bf W}_{i}{\bf W}_{i}^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|{\bf W}_{i}|^2}
\]
have the same LSD, and
\[
\lim\limits_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}{p}=  \lim\limits_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p} = \theta.
\]
Moreover, the LSD of  $3 \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_{i}|^2}{p}\cdot\frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{{\bf W}_{i}{\bf W}_{i}^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|{\bf W}_{i}|^2}$ is generated by Theorem 2.3 of \cite{XiaandZheng20182}.
Therefore, the proof of Theorem \ref{thm: theorem for the TVAPA asynt} is complete.

Finally, we only need to show the proofs of \eqref{eq: min of Wi2} and \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}.
Notice that \eqref{eq: min of Wi2} follows naturally from the proof of \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX}.
To prove \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}, by the normality of $R_{i1}^{(q)}$, $R_{i2}^{(q)}$, and $R_{i3}^{(q)}$, Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu}, and $\max\limits_{1\leq i \leq n, 1\leq q\leq  p} nh(s_{T_i}^{(q)} - t_i) \to 0 $ almost surely, we have
\[
E(R_{i1}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i1}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh^2}),
\]
\[E(R_{i2}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{n}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i2}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh}),
\]
and
\[E(R_{i3}^{(q)}) = o(\frac{1}{n}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i3}^{(q)}) = o(\frac{1}{n}).
\]
Let $R_{i}^{(q)} = R_{i1}^{(q)} + R_{i2}^{(q)} + R_{i3}^{(q)}$; thus, by $C_p$ inequality and the normality of $R_{i}^{(q)} $, we have for any $\kappa\geq 1$, 
\[
 E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) < Cn^{-1} ~~\text{and}~~ E|R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |^{2\kappa} \leq Cn^{-\kappa},
\]
for all $i, q$.
Hence,  it follows that for any $\varepsilon >0$ and $\kappa \geq 1$,
\[
\begin{split}
&P\left(\max\limits_{i,q} \sqrt{p}| R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |\geq \varepsilon\right) \\
&\leq \sum\limits_{i,q}\frac{p^{\kappa} E| R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |^{2\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2\kappa}}\\
&\leq C\cdot \frac{Mp\cdot p^{\kappa} \cdot n^{-\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2\kappa}} = O(p^{2-\kappa\beta/(1-\beta)}).
\end{split}
\]
We choose $\kappa$ large enough such that $\kappa\beta/(1-\beta)- 2 > 1$.
Therefore, \eqref{eq: asynchronous key} holds by the Borel--Cantelli lemma.
\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$ \hbox{} \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Decompose asynchronous pre-averaged returns into a synchronous part W_i plus remainders, reduce to the synchronous case via Lemma D.1. The key step shows the remainders are o(1/sqrt(p)) uniformly by moment bounds and Borel-Cantelli.

nodes.statement: \min\limits_{1\leq i\leq M} |\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}^*_{2i}|^2 \geq C,
nodes.label: eq: xy same require in AT

nodes.name: Asynchronous noise vanishes
nodes.statement: \max\limits_{1\leq i \leq M, 1\leq j \leq p} \sqrt{p}|\Delta (\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}^{*})^{(j)} | \to 0, ~~~\text{almost surely,}
nodes.label: eq: xy same require in AT done

nodes.name: Lower bound on W_i
nodes.statement: \min\limits_{1\leq i \leq M}|{\bf W}_{i}|^2\geq C,

nodes.name: Zheng-Li Lemma 1: perturbation of sample covariance ESD
nodes.statement: (Lemma 1 in \cite{ZhengandLi20112}). Suppose that for each $p$, ${\bf v}_l = (v_l^1, \cdots, v_l^p)^\mathrm{T}$ and $\bm w_l = (w_l^1,\cdots,w_l^p)^{\mathrm{T}},l =1, \cdots, m$, are all $p$-dimensional vectors. Define \[\bm{\widetilde{S}}_m = \sum_{l=1}^m (\bm v_l + \bm w_l)(\bm v_l + \bm w_l)^\mathrm{T} \text{~and~} \bm S_m = \sum_{l=1}^mw_l(w_l)^\mathrm{T}.\] Suppose the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{itemize} \item $m = m(p)$ with $\lim_{p\to\infty} p/m = c >0$; \item there exists a sequence $\epsilon_p = o(1/\sqrt{p})$ such that for all $p$ and all $l$, all the entries of $\bm v_l$ are bounded by $\epsilon_p$ in absolute value; \item $\lim\sup_{p\to\infty}\begin{rm}tr\end{rm}(\bm S_m)/p<\infty$ almost surely. \end{itemize} Then $L(F^{\bm{\widetilde{S}}_m}, F^{\bm S_m}) \to 0$ almost surely, where for any two probability distribution functions $F$ and $G$, $L(F, G)$ denotes the Levy distance between them.
assumptions: there exists a sequence $\epsilon_p = o(1/\sqrt{p})$ such that for all $p$ and all $l$, all the entries of $\bm v_l$ are bounded by $\epsilon_p$ in absolute value
nodes.statement_short: Small (o(1/sqrt p)) perturbations of the vectors do not change the limiting ESD in Levy distance.
nodes.label: lem: appendix B lemma 1

nodes.name: Recall averaged return
nodes.statement:
Recall that
\[\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i} =  \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}\Delta_{2i,j}{\bf X} +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}\Delta_{2i-1,j}{\bf X},\]
where $a_{i,j} = 1-\frac{j-1}{L_i},  b_{i,j} = \frac{j-1}{L_i}$, and $\Delta_{i,j}{\bf X} = {\bf X}_{T_{i-1}+j} - {\bf X}_{T_{i-1}+j - 1}$.

nodes.name: Split into diffusion and drift parts
nodes.statement_short: Split into diffusion and drift parts

nodes.name: Rewrite Sigma~
nodes.statement:
Using the above notation, $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ can be rewritten as
\[\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} = \frac{p}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{\Delta\overline{{\bf X}}_{2i}\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2} = \frac{p}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \frac{({\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i)({\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i)^{\mathrm{T}} }{|{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}{\bf Z}_i|^2}.\]

nodes.name: Drift part uniformly bounded
nodes.statement: By the boundedness of $|\mu_t^{(l)}|$ and $|\gamma_t|$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu} and \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma}, and the equally spaced transaction durations $\Delta s_{i,j}$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_duration}, there exists $C>0$ such that $|{\bf V}_i^{(l)}|\leq C/\sqrt{N}$ for all $i=1,\cdots,N,l=1,\cdots, p$, which indicates that the $|{\bf V}_i|$ are uniformly bounded.

nodes.name: Norm concentration of Lambda Z_i
Norm concentration with drift
Conclude via Zheng-Li argument
nodes.statement: By the same arguments used in the proof of Theorem 2 in \cite{ZhengandLi20112}, we can show that Proposition \ref{prop: convergence of tilde sigma} holds.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$

nodes.name: ICV ESD convergence
nodes.statement:
The convergence of $F^{ICV}$ follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:LSD_bH} and the fact that
\[F^{\textrm{ICV}}(x) = F^{\breve{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}}\left(\frac{x}{\int_0^1\gamma_t^2dt}\right) \hspace{0.5cm} \text{for all~} x\geq 0.\]

nodes.name: Decompose the scale
nodes.statement:
We proceed to show the convergence of $1/p\cdot \sum_{i=1}^N|\Delta \overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2$.
Write $\Delta \overline{\bf{X}}_{2i} = \sqrt{w_i}(\boldsymbol{\Lambda} {\bf Z}_i + {\bf V}_i)$ as in \eqref{eq: expression of delta wbx}; then
\[
\dfrac 1p |\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{2i}|^2 = \dfrac 1p \sum_{i=1}^N w_i |{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda} {\bf Z}_i|^2 =\sum_{i=1}^N Ew_i + \sum_{i=1}^N (w_i - Ew_i) + \varepsilon,
\]
where $\varepsilon = \sum_{i = 1}^N w_i (p^{-1} |{\bf V}_i + \boldsymbol{\Lambda} {\bf Z}_i|^2 - 1)$.

nodes.name: Error and fluctuation terms vanish
nodes.statement:
First, almost surely, that $\max\limits_{i,n} (N w_i)$ is bounded follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma} and \eqref{asm:bdd_duration}.
Thus, combining this with the convergence of \eqref{eq: order of v pluz z}, the error term $\varepsilon$ converges to 0 almost surely.
Besides, $\sum_{i=1}^N (w_i - E(w_i))$ converges to zero almost surely by the Kolmogorov strong law of large numbers and the boundedness of $\max\limits_{i,n} (N w_i)$.

nodes.name: Claim: N E(w_i) approximates w_s
nodes.statement:
Next, we show that there exists a piecewise continuous process $(w_s)$ with finite jumps such that
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^N \int_{(2i-2)/n}^{2i/n}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds =0,
\]
where $w_s = (\dfrac 13 + \dfrac 16 f_{2,s}^*)\cdot (\gamma_s^*)^2$.
Suppose that $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$, and $(f_{2,s}^*)$ have a finite number of jumps J in total. 
For each $j = 1,\cdots, J$, there exists an $\ell_j$ such that the $j$th jump falls in the interval $((2\ell_j - 2)/n, 2\ell_j/n]$.
Then
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\sum_{i=1}^N\int_{(2i-2)/n}^{2i/n}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds\\
=&\sum\limits_{\ell_j \in \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2\ell_j-2}{n}}^{\frac{2\ell_j}{n}}|N E(w_{\ell_j}) - w_s|ds +
\sum\limits_{i \notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}|N E(w_i) - w_s|ds\\
:= &D_1 + D_2.\\
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
As $(N w_{\ell_j})$, $|\gamma_s^*|$, and $|f_{2,s}^*|$ are bounded, for any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, we have
\[|D_1|\leq \frac{2}{n}JC <\epsilon.\]
Notice that
\[
E \left(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 \right)= \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}^2}\big) + \frac{1}{2}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\big),
\]
and
\[ E\left( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1
,j}^2 \right)  = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}^2}\big) - \frac{1}{2} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\big).
\]
For the second term $D_2$, because $(\gamma_t^*)$, $f_{1,s}^*$,  and $f_{2,s}^*$ are continuous in $[(2i-2)/n, 2i/n]$ when $i \notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}$, and by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_ICV} and \eqref{asm:moment_L}, $(\gamma_t)$, $(f_{1,s})$,  and $(f_{2,s})$ uniformly converge to $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$,  and $(f_{2,s}^*)$, respectively.
For any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n,p$, we have
\[|\gamma_t^* - \gamma_{2i/n}|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{and}~~ |f_{2, 2i/n}^* - f_{2, t}^*|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{for all}  ~~t \in [\frac{2i-2}{n},\frac{2i}{n} ],\]
for $i = 1,\cdots, N$ and $|\gamma_t - \gamma_t^*|<\epsilon$ for all $t\in [0,1]$.
Define
\[
\begin{split}
w_i^* &= \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2\int_{s_{T_{2i-1} + j -1}}^{s_{T_{2i-1} + j}}(\gamma_t^*)^2dt +  \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\int_{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j -1} }^{ s_{T_{2i-2} + j}}(\gamma_t^*)^2dt,\\
\widetilde{w}_i^*&= (\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2 \frac{1}{nL_{2i}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 + (\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2 \frac{1}{nL_{2i-1}}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1,j}^2\\
\text{and}~~~
 \widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^*&=(\gamma_{2i/n}^*)^2\cdot\frac{2}{n}\bigg(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}f_{2, 2i/n}^*\bigg).
\end{split}
\]
For all large $n$, because $|\gamma_t|\leq C$ and $1\leq L_i< L^*$, for any $i, t$, we have
\[
\begin{split}
&|D_2| \\
\leq& \sum\limits_{i}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}N|E(w_i) - E(w_i^*)|ds + \sum\limits_{i\notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}N| E(w_i^*) - E(\widetilde{w}_i^*)|ds \\
+&\sum\limits_{i}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}| NE(\widetilde{w}_i^*) - N\widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^*|ds  +\sum\limits_{i\notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}}\int_{\frac{2i-2}{n}}^{\frac{2i}{n}}| N\widetilde{\widetilde{w}}_i^* - w_s|ds\\
\to& 0, ~~~\text{almost surely.}
\end{split}
\]
This completes the proof of \eqref{eq: convergence of Vi plus lambda Zi}.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$

nodes.name: Split at jumps into D_1 + D_2
nodes.statement_short: Split at jumps into D_1 + D_2

nodes.name: Bound D_1
nodes.statement:
As $(N w_{\ell_j})$, $|\gamma_s^*|$, and $|f_{2,s}^*|$ are bounded, for any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, we have
\[|D_1|\leq \frac{2}{n}JC <\epsilon.\]

nodes.name: Expected weight sums
nodes.statement:
Notice that
\[
E \left(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i}}a_{2i,j}^2 \right)= \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}^2}\big) + \frac{1}{2}E\big(\frac{1}{L_{2i}}\big),
\]
and
\[ E\left( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\sum_{j = 1}^{L_{2i-1}}b_{2i-1
,j}^2 \right)  = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}^2}\big) - \frac{1}{2} E\big( \frac{1}{L_{2i-1}}\big).
\]

nodes.name: Continuity on non-jump intervals
nodes.statement:
For the second term $D_2$, because $(\gamma_t^*)$, $f_{1,s}^*$,  and $f_{2,s}^*$ are continuous in $[(2i-2)/n, 2i/n]$ when $i \notin \{\ell_1,\cdots,\ell_J\}$, and by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_ICV} and \eqref{asm:moment_L}, $(\gamma_t)$, $(f_{1,s})$,  and $(f_{2,s})$ uniformly converge to $(\gamma_t^*)$, $(f_{1,s}^*)$,  and $(f_{2,s}^*)$, respectively.
For any $\epsilon >0$ and for sufficiently large $n,p$, we have
\[|\gamma_t^* - \gamma_{2i/n}|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{and}~~ |f_{2, 2i/n}^* - f_{2, t}^*|<\epsilon, ~~ \text{for all}  ~~t \in [\frac{2i-2}{n},\frac{2i}{n} ],\]
for $i = 1,\cdots, N$ and $|\gamma_t - \gamma_t^*|<\epsilon$ for all $t\in [0,1]$.

nodes.name: Bound D_2 and conclude
Reduce to same LSD of noisy and latent
nodes.statement:
To prove the convergence of $F^{\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}}$, we shall show that
\[
\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}} = \frac{p}{M} \sum_{i=1}^M\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}(\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i})^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2}~~~\text{and}~~~
\widetilde{\widetilde{\bm{\Xi}}} := \frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2}
\]
have the same LSD.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to same LSD of noisy and latent

nodes.name: Suffices: noise ratio vanishes
Sub-goal: lower bound
Decompose pre-averaged return
nodes.statement:
By equation \eqref{eqn:Delta_V}, we decompose $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}$ as follows:
\begin{align*}
\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}= & \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\left(\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-1)h + j} - \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h}\right) - \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\left( \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+j} -  \overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h}\right) \notag\\
= & \sum_{l=1}^{2h}\left (1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)\Delta\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+l}\notag\\
= & \sum_{l=1}^{2h}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}a_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X}\notag\\
&+\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l|}{h} \right )\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}}b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}{\bf X}.\\
\end{align*}

nodes.name: Rewrite with psi_i, Z~_i, V~_i
WLOG independence
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\gamma_t$ and ${\bf W}_t$ are independent, which leads to the fact that each entry of $\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i$ is i.i.d. standard normal.

nodes.name: Norm concentration otherwise
Scale as sum of psi_i
Triangle-type lower bound
nodes.statement:
Thus, from equation \eqref{eq: expression for tbwX},  we have
\[
|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 = |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i + \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 \geq |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i|^2 + |\psi_i|\cdot| \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 - 2|\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i| | \sqrt{\psi_i}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|.
\]

nodes.name: Establish lower bound
nodes.statement:
Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_sigma} implies that for all $i$, there exists $C'$ such that$|\psi_i|\geq C'h/n.$
Taking this together with Assumption \eqref{asm:dim_windows} and Equation \eqref{eq: norm convergeb=nce of tbZ}, there exists $C^*>0$ such that for all $n$ large enough,
\[
\min\limits_{1\leq i \leq m}|\psi_i|\cdot| \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\widetilde{\bf{Z}}_i|^2 \geq C^*.
\]
Moreover, $\max_i |\widetilde{\bf{V}}_i| =O(\sqrt{p}\times h/n) = o(1)$ follows from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu}.
Therefore \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX} follows.

nodes.name: Next sub-goal: noise vanishes
rho-mixing of averaged noise and conclude
nodes.statement:
Observe that $(\bar{\varepsilon}_i^{(j)}) = (1/L_i\sum_{k=1}^{L_i}\varepsilon_{i,k}^{(j)})$ is also a $\rho$-mixing sequence following from Definition \ref{def: rho-misiing}, and the $\rho$-mixing coefficients $\bar{\rho}^j(r)$ based on $(\bar{\varepsilon}_i^{(j)})$ have the same order as $\rho^j(r)$ by the boundedness of $L_i$ from Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_L}.
Therefore, \eqref{eq: sqrtt p delta twbe} follows by the same process used in (C.7) of \cite{XiaandZheng20182}, which, together with \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX}, implies that \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x} holds.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$
nodes.statement_short: rho-mixing of averaged noise and conclude

nodes.name: Expand noisy scale
nodes.statement:
Note that
\[\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{Y}}}_{2i}|^2 = \sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}|^2 + 2\sum_{i=1}^M\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^{\mathrm{T}}\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i} + \sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}|^2.
\]

nodes.name: Noise term vanishes
nodes.statement: The convergence of \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x} implies that $\sum_{i=1}^M|\Delta \widetilde{\overline{\bm{\varepsilon}}}_{2i}|^2/p \to 0$ almost surely.

nodes.name: Remaining goals
Reduce to integral approximation
nodes.statement:
To show \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}, by \eqref{eq: psii plus error term}, it suffices to show that
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^M\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds =0,
\]
almost surely.

nodes.name: Split at jumps
nodes.statement:
Suppose that  $\gamma_t^*$ has $J$ jumps at $\{\tau_1,\cdots,\tau_J\}$; then
\begin{align*}
&\sum_{i=1}^M\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} |M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds\\
=&\sum\limits_{i \in \{\tau_1,\cdots,\tau_J\}}\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds \\
&+ \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1,\cdots,\tau_J\}}\int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}}|M\psi_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_s^*)^2|ds \\
:= &\Delta_1 + \Delta_2.
\end{align*}

nodes.name: Bound Delta_1
nodes.statement: For any $\epsilon > 0$ and for sufficiently large $n$, $|\Delta_1| \leq \epsilon$ follows from the boundedness of $|M\psi_i|$ and $\gamma_t^*$.

nodes.name: Decompose Delta_2
nodes.statement:
For the second term, $\Delta_2$, by defining $\psi_i^*$ by replacing $\gamma_t$ with $\gamma_t^*$ from the definition of $\psi_i$, we have
\[
|\Delta_2| \leq \Delta_{21} + \Delta_{22} + \Delta_{23} +\Delta_{24},
\]
where
\[
\begin{split}
\Delta_{21} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} |M\psi_i - M\psi_i^*|ds,\\
\Delta_{22} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M\psi_i^* - M(\gamma_{(2i-2)/h}^*)^2A_i|ds,\\
\Delta_{23} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M(\gamma_{(2i-2)/h}^*)^2A_i - M(\gamma_{s}^*)^2A_i |ds,\\
\Delta_{24} &:= \sum\limits_{i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}} \int_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}}^{s_{T_{2ih}}} | M(\gamma_{s}^*)^2A_i - \frac{1}{3}(\gamma_{s}^*)^2 |ds,
\end{split}
\]
and
\[
\begin{split}
A_i := &\frac{1}{h^2} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}} a_{2ih,j}^2 \Delta s_{2ih,j} + \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \Big[1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h}+ \\
&\hspace{1cm}+\frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h}b_{(2i-2)h+l,j} \Big]^2\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} .
\end{split}
\]

nodes.name: Orders of A_i components
nodes.statement:
We further decompose $A_i$ as $A_i = A_{i1} +  A_{i2} + A_{i3}+ A_{i4}$, where
\begin{align*}
A_{i1} &:= \frac{1}{h^2} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}} a_{2ih,j}^2 \Delta s_{2ih,j} = O(\frac{1}{nh^2}),\\
A_{i2} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)^2\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j}= \frac{2h}{3n} + o(\frac{h}{n}),\\
A_{i3} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \frac{2}{h}\left(1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} \right)(|h-l+1| - |h-l|) \\
&\cdot b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} = O(\frac{1}{n}),\\
A_{i4} &:= \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}} \frac{1}{h^2}(|h-l+1| - |h-l|)^2b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^2\Delta s_{(2i-2)h+l,j} \\
&= O(\frac{1}{nh}),
\end{align*}
follow from the boundedness of $L_i$ both below and above, and $\Delta s_{i,j} = O(1/n)$ by Assumption \eqref{asm:interval}.

nodes.name: Bound Delta_2 terms
nodes.statement:
As $(\gamma_t^*)$ is continuous in $[s_{T_{(2i-2)h}}, s_{T_{2ih}}]$ when $i \notin \{\tau_1, \cdots, \tau_J\}$, $(\gamma_t)$ uniformly converges to $(\gamma_t^*)$  by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_sigma}, and $\psi_i^* = O(h/n)$ by Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_gamma} and \eqref{asm:bdd_L}, for any $\epsilon >0 $ and sufficiently large $n,p$, it is easy to show that
\[
|MA_i - 1/3|\leq \epsilon ~~~\text{and}~~~\max\{\Delta_{21},\Delta_{22}, \Delta_{23},\Delta_{24}  \}<C\epsilon.
\]
This completes the proof of \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}.

nodes.name: Cross term and conclude
nodes.statement: Finally, \eqref{eq: twbX plus twbe} follows from \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx} and \eqref{eq: convergence og delta epsilon divided by delta x}.\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$

nodes.name: WLOG and setting
nodes.statement:
Without of generality, we may assume that  $\gamma_t$ is independent of ${\bf W}_t$.
Suppose that we have $L_i^{(q)}(\geq 1)$ observations for each stock $q$ at recording time $t_i = i/n$, for $q = 1,2,\cdots, p$ and $i = 1,2,\cdots, n$.

nodes.name: Recall notation
nodes.statement:
Recall that for any process $({\bf V}_t)$, $V_{i,j}^{(q)}$ denote the observation of the $j$th transaction for stock $q$ during time interval $(t_{i-1}, t_i]$,
and the true transaction time of $V_{i,j}^{(q)}$ is denoted as $s_{T_{i-1}+j}^{(q)}$, for $j = 1,\cdots, L_i^{(q)}$ satisfying $t_{i-1} \leq s_{T_{i-1}}^{(q)}< s_{T_{i-1} + 1}^{(q)}<\cdots < s_{T_{i-1} + L_i^{(q)}}^{(q)} = s_{T_i}^{(q)} \leq t_i$.

nodes.name: Asynchronous averages and increments
nodes.statement:
Under asynchronous trading conditions, the average of multiple observations at each recording time $t_i$ is denoted by
\[
\overline{\bf{V}}^*_i := \left(\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(1)}}\frac{1}{L_i^{(1)}}V_{i,j}^{(1)}, \cdots, \sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(p)}}\frac{1}{L_i^{(p)}}V_{i,j}^{(p)} \right)^{{\mathrm{T}}};
\]
thus, the increment at trading time $t_i$ becomes
\[\Delta\overline{{\bf V}}^*_i :=  \begin{pmatrix}
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(1)}}a_{i,j}^{(1)}\Delta_{i,j}^{(1)}V +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}^{(1)}}b_{i-1,j}^{(1)}\Delta_{i-1,j}^{(1)}V\\
\vdots\\
\sum_{j=1}^{L_i^{(p)}}a_{i,j}^{(p)}\Delta_{i,j}^{(p)}V +   \sum_{j=1}^{L_{i-1}^{(p)}}b_{i-1,j}^{(p)}\Delta_{i-1,j}^{(p)}V\\
\end{pmatrix},\]
where $a_{i,j}^{(q)} = 1 - \frac{j-1}{L_i^{(q)}}$, $b_{i,j}^{(q)} =  \frac{j-1}{L_i^{(q)}}$ and  $\Delta_{i,j}^{(q)}X = X_{i, j}^{(q)} -  X_{i, j-1}^{(q)}$, for $q = 1,2,\cdots,p$.

nodes.name: Reduce to two bounds
Only lower bound needed
nodes.statement: We only need to prove \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT}, as \eqref{eq: xy same require in AT done} holds straightforwardly from the proof of \eqref{eq: sqrtt p delta twbe} given earlier.

nodes.name: Decompose return into R1 + M + R2
nodes.statement:
By a similar decomposition to that used in \eqref{eq: expression for tbwX}, the return based on the pre-averaged (latent) price can be decomposed as
\[
\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^* = \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-1)h+j}^* - \frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{h}\overline{\bf{X}}_{(2i-2)h+j}^* = {\bf R}_{i1} + {\bf M}_{i} + {\bf R}_{i2},
\]
where ${\bf M}_i = (M_{i}^{(1)}, \cdots, M_{i}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$, ${\bf R}_{i\ell} = (R_{i\ell}^{(1)}, \cdots, R_{i\ell}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$ for $\ell = 1, 2$, and their $q$th components have the form
\begin{align*}
R_{i1}^{(q)} = &\frac{1}{h}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{2ih}^{(q)}}a_{2ih,j}^{(q)}\Delta_{2ih,j}^{(q)}X,\\
M_{i}^{(q)} = & \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \sum_{j = 1}^{L_{(2i-2)h+l}^{(q)} }c_{l,h} \Delta_{(2i-2)h + l,j}^{(q)}X,\\
R_{i2}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{L_{(2i-2)h + l}^{(q)}} \left[ \frac{|h-l+1| - |h-l|}{h}
b_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^{(q)}\right]\Delta_{(2i-2)h+l,j}^{(q)} X,
\end{align*}
where $c_{l,h} = 1 - \frac{|h-l+1|}{h} $.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose return into R1 + M + R2

nodes.name: Split M into W + R3
nodes.statement:
Note that $M_i^{(q)}$ can be reduced to
\[
\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} \cdot (X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)}}^{(q)} - X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l - 1} }^{(q)}}^{(q)}).
\]
We further decompose $M_i^{(q)}$ as $W_i^{(q)} + R_{i3}^{(q)}$, where
\begin{align*}
W_{i}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} (X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l}}^{(q)} -  X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l - 1}}^{(q)}),\\
R_{i3}^{(q)} = &\sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} c_{l,h} \left(  X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)}}^{(q)} - X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l} }^{(q)} + X_{t_{(2i-2)h + l -1}}^{(q)} -  X_{s_{T_{(2i-2)h + l - 1}}^{(q)}}^{(q)}  \right),
\end{align*}
and $X_{t_i}^{(q)}$ denotes the log price for stock $q$ at recording time $t_i$.  Let ${\bf W}_i = (W_{i}^{(1)}, \cdots, W_{i}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$, ${\bf R}_{i3} = (R_{i3}^{(1)}, \cdots, R_{i3}^{(q)})^{{\mathrm{T}}}$.
Thus, $\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{2i}^*  = {\bf W}_i + {\bf R}_{i1} + {\bf R}_{i2}  + {\bf R}_{i3} $.

nodes.name: Reduces to synchronous setting
nodes.statement:
As 
\[{\bf W}_{i} = \sum_{l=1}^{2h-1} \left(1-\frac{|h-l+1|}{h}\right) \Delta {\bf X}_{(2i-2)h + l}^*,
\]
and 
\[
\Delta {\bf X}_{(2i-2)h + l}^* = \begin{pmatrix}
X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l }}}^{(1)} -X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l-1 }}}^{(1)}\\
 \vdots\\
  X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l }}}^{(p)} -X_{t_{T_{(2i-2)h +l-1 }}}^{(p)}\\
  \end{pmatrix},
\]
it reduces to the synchronous setting.

nodes.name: Scale of W_i converges
nodes.statement:
Using a similar argument to that in \eqref{eq: convergence of sum of TWBx}, we have
\[ \lim\limits_{p\to\infty} \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p} = \theta.
\]

nodes.name: Reduce to bounds on W_i and remainders
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bounds on W_i and remainders

nodes.name: Apply Lemma D.1 and Xia-Zheng Theorem 2.3
nodes.statement:
Further, using \eqref{eq: min of Wi2}, \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}, and Lemma \ref{lem: appendix B lemma 1}, we obtain that
\[
3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}{p} \cdot \frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^* (\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*)^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}
~~\text{and}~~3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p}\cdot\frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{{\bf W}_{i}{\bf W}_{i}^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|{\bf W}_{i}|^2}
\]
have the same LSD, and
\[
\lim\limits_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |\Delta\widetilde{\overline{\bf{X}}}_{i2}^*|^2}{p}=  \lim\limits_{p\to\infty} 3\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_i|^2}{p} = \theta.
\]
Moreover, the LSD of  $3 \frac{\sum_{i=1}^M |{\bf W}_{i}|^2}{p}\cdot\frac{p}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\frac{{\bf W}_{i}{\bf W}_{i}^{{\mathrm{T}}}}{|{\bf W}_{i}|^2}$ is generated by Theorem 2.3 of \cite{XiaandZheng20182}.
Therefore, the proof of Theorem \ref{thm: theorem for the TVAPA asynt} is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma D.1 and Xia-Zheng Theorem 2.3

nodes.name: Remaining bounds
nodes.statement:
Finally, we only need to show the proofs of \eqref{eq: min of Wi2} and \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}.
Notice that \eqref{eq: min of Wi2} follows naturally from the proof of \eqref{eq: minimun of twbX}.

nodes.name: Moments of remainders
nodes.statement:
To prove \eqref{eq: asynchronous key}, by the normality of $R_{i1}^{(q)}$, $R_{i2}^{(q)}$, and $R_{i3}^{(q)}$, Assumption \eqref{asm:bdd_mu}, and $\max\limits_{1\leq i \leq n, 1\leq q\leq  p} nh(s_{T_i}^{(q)} - t_i) \to 0 $ almost surely, we have
\[
E(R_{i1}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i1}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh^2}),
\]
\[E(R_{i2}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{n}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i2}^{(q)}) = O(\frac{1}{nh}),
\]
and
\[E(R_{i3}^{(q)}) = o(\frac{1}{n}), ~~~\begin{rm} Var \end{rm}(R_{i3}^{(q)}) = o(\frac{1}{n}).
\]

nodes.name: Higher moment bound
nodes.statement:
Let $R_{i}^{(q)} = R_{i1}^{(q)} + R_{i2}^{(q)} + R_{i3}^{(q)}$; thus, by $C_p$ inequality and the normality of $R_{i}^{(q)} $, we have for any $\kappa\geq 1$, 
\[
 E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) < Cn^{-1} ~~\text{and}~~ E|R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |^{2\kappa} \leq Cn^{-\kappa},
\]
for all $i, q$.

nodes.name: Union bound and Borel-Cantelli
nodes.statement:
Hence,  it follows that for any $\varepsilon >0$ and $\kappa \geq 1$,
\[
\begin{split}
&P\left(\max\limits_{i,q} \sqrt{p}| R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |\geq \varepsilon\right) \\
&\leq \sum\limits_{i,q}\frac{p^{\kappa} E| R_{i}^{(q)} - E(R_{i}^{(q)} ) |^{2\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2\kappa}}\\
&\leq C\cdot \frac{Mp\cdot p^{\kappa} \cdot n^{-\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2\kappa}} = O(p^{2-\kappa\beta/(1-\beta)}).
\end{split}
\]
We choose $\kappa$ large enough such that $\kappa\beta/(1-\beta)- 2 > 1$.
Therefore, \eqref{eq: asynchronous key} holds by the Borel--Cantelli lemma.
\hspace{\fill}$\blacksquare$
